description.key_ids: Test secrets, each the SHA-256 of the ASCII label `ori alert-delivery-transport/v1 <name> test secret` written as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters, with the key_id derived by HKDF-SHA256 over the secret's UTF-8 bytes. The HMAC key is the same UTF-8 bytes. Test secrets only.
description.runtime_test_keys: Ed25519 report keys, each seeded by the SHA-256 of its `seed_label`, that sign the record bodies. Test keys only.
description.registry: The receiver's own registry, shared by every request case: each client's key_ids, the devices it may forward for and the owners on whose behalf it may; and each report-key enrolment, binding a key to a device and to the owner it names, and `revoked` true for a key since revoked. Each key is its own epoch.
description.requests: Requests as an exact request line, every header received in order, and body, with the HMAC input as hex wherever X-Ori-Alert-Sent-At-Ms carries an integer's own spelling, and the receiver's verdict at checks 1 to 8 of Order. `receiver` gives the receiver's clock, the (client_id, key_id, nonce) triples it already holds, and the records it holds verified, each as stored or conflict. A verdict names its check (null when every check passes), HTTP status, whether the response is authenticated, and the exact response body; a refusal names its reason, and an accepted request check 8's verdict: stored, conflict, duplicate or lower_count. A case that fails more than one check declares `precedence`.
description.responses: A response to a request whose digest is `request_digest`, with the gateway's action. A case on a row of the table names it as `row`; a case that retires nothing names the way as `retires_nothing`: another_digest, unparsable, unpaired or unauthenticated.
description.config: gateway-config/v2 documents, judged under the alert_delivery load rules: rule 1 on the forwarding keys, rules 6 to 8, and accepted cases. Every case keeps rules 2 to 5 satisfied. A refused case names the rule; an accepted enabled case says whether forwarding is configured.

requests.name: accepted_submission
requests.note: A submission observation for a device the client may forward for, under the key enrolled for it, sent 2000 ms before the receiver's clock: stored.

requests.name: accepted_tally
requests.note: A withholding tally: the hop carries either kind of record alike.

requests.name: accepted_client_b
requests.note: The second client, under its own secret, for its own device.

requests.name: accepted_retry_duplicate
requests.note: A retry of accepted_submission after its response was lost: the same body and digest under a fresh sent_at_ms, nonce and HMAC, with the first nonce held and the record held: duplicate.

requests.name: accepted_conflict_stored
requests.note: Different bytes under an observation identity the receiver holds: held as conflict, answered stored.

requests.name: accepted_lower_count_superseded
requests.note: A tally whose count is below the greatest held for its key: lower_count, answered superseded.

requests.name: accepted_moved_device_new_key
requests.note: The moved device, forwarded by its new site's client, under the key enrolled since it moved, which names that site.

requests.name: accepted_skew_at_bound_past
requests.note: sent_at_ms exactly 300000 ms before the receiver's clock: within the bound.

requests.name: accepted_skew_at_bound_future
requests.note: sent_at_ms exactly 300000 ms after the receiver's clock: within the bound.

requests.name: accepted_nonce_held_for_other_client
requests.note: The nonce is held, but under another (client_id, key_id): the reservation is of the triple, so this is no replay.

requests.name: accepted_client_id_escaped
requests.note: A client identifier with a space, a quotation mark and a backslash, all printable ASCII: its HMAC input carries them escaped under gateway-mqtt-canonical-json/v1.

requests.name: accepted_client_id_128
requests.note: A client identifier of 128 characters, the bound.

requests.name: accepted_32_headers
requests.note: Host, Content-Length, Content-Type, the six required headers and 23 others: 32 headers, the bound.

requests.name: accepted_header_1024_bytes
requests.note: One header of exactly 1024 bytes, counted as its name, `: ` and its value.

requests.name: accepted_content_type_other_case
requests.note: Content-Type Application/Octet-Stream: the media type is compared without regard to case.

requests.name: accepted_header_names_other_case
requests.note: Required headers named in other case: x-ori-alert-nonce and AUTHORIZATION. Names are compared without regard to case.

requests.name: check1_33_headers
requests.note: 33 headers, Host and Content-Length counted, one past the bound; every required header is present once and well formed.

requests.name: check1_header_over_1024_bytes
requests.note: One header of 1025 bytes, counted as its name, `: ` and its value.

requests.name: check1_content_length_mismatch
requests.note: Content-Length one more than the body's length; every other header matches the body.

requests.name: check1_content_length_absent
requests.note: No Content-Length header: it must be present, and equal to the body's length.

requests.name: check1_content_length_short
requests.note: Content-Length one less than the body's length.

requests.name: precedence_1_over_2_long_path
requests.note: A request line of 1025 bytes made by a longer path: check 1 is first, and the target, not exactly the path, would fail check 2.

requests.name: check1_body_over_limit
requests.note: A body of 4097 bytes, one past the bound: a record padded with spaces, its digest header and HMAC over the padded bytes. The padding also makes it not_canonical at check 6.

requests.name: check2_query
requests.note: The request target is the path with a query: not exactly the path.

requests.name: check2_method_put
requests.note: The method PUT on the exact path. The HMAC input names POST, as it always does, and is valid; only the method refuses it.

requests.name: check2_method_lower
requests.note: The method post in lower case: HTTP methods are case-sensitive, so not POST.

requests.name: check2_client_empty
requests.note: An empty X-Ori-Alert-Client. The registry holds no such client, so checks 3 and 7 would refuse it too; check 2 is first.

requests.name: check2_client_129
requests.note: An X-Ori-Alert-Client of 129 characters, one past the bound.

requests.name: check2_client_control
requests.note: An X-Ori-Alert-Client holding a DEL character, outside printable ASCII.

requests.name: check2_key_id_upper
requests.note: An X-Ori-Alert-Key-Id in upper-case hexadecimal: not of its form. The HMAC is over the header as sent.

requests.name: check2_sent_zero
requests.note: X-Ori-Alert-Sent-At-Ms of 0, below 1. The HMAC is valid over the integer 0, so only freshness would also refuse it.

requests.name: check2_sent_over_max
requests.note: X-Ori-Alert-Sent-At-Ms of 9007199254740992, one past 2^53 - 1, with a valid HMAC over that integer.

requests.name: check2_sent_leading_zero
requests.note: X-Ori-Alert-Sent-At-Ms with a leading zero: no integer's own spelling, so neither the HMAC input nor freshness has a sent_at_ms, and Authorization is a fixed well-formed value.

requests.name: check2_nonce_upper
requests.note: An X-Ori-Alert-Nonce in upper-case hexadecimal.

requests.name: check2_nonce_short
requests.note: An X-Ori-Alert-Nonce of 30 hexadecimal characters, 15 bytes.

requests.name: check2_digest_upper
requests.note: An X-Ori-Alert-Record-Digest in upper-case hexadecimal.

requests.name: check2_digest_mismatch
requests.note: A well-formed X-Ori-Alert-Record-Digest over other bytes than the body, and an HMAC over the header as sent: only the recomputed digest refuses it.

requests.name: check2_auth_scheme
requests.note: An Authorization header with a valid HMAC under another scheme name.

requests.name: check2_auth_upper
requests.note: An Authorization header whose HMAC is the right value in upper-case hexadecimal.

requests.name: check2_nonce_missing
requests.note: No X-Ori-Alert-Nonce header: no HMAC input exists, and Authorization is a fixed well-formed value. Neither check 4 nor check 5 has its inputs.

requests.name: check2_authorization_missing
requests.note: No Authorization header: a missing header is a header form, at check 2, and no HMAC input exists.

requests.name: check2_client_twice
requests.note: X-Ori-Alert-Client twice, both copies the same value: each required header is present exactly once. No HMAC input exists, and checks 3, 4, 5 and 7 lack a single client identifier.

requests.name: check2_client_twice_different
requests.note: X-Ori-Alert-Client twice with different values, the first the client whose key_id and device the request carries and the last another client the registry holds. There is no single client identifier, so neither check 3 nor check 7 has its input: a judge that kept the last value would refuse it at 3 and 7 as well, and one that kept the first would accept it there.

requests.name: check2_nonce_twice_other_case
requests.note: X-Ori-Alert-Nonce twice, once in other case: names compared without regard to case are the same header, present twice. No HMAC input exists.

requests.name: check2_content_type_missing
requests.note: No Content-Type header.

requests.name: check2_content_type_parameter
requests.note: Content-Type application/octet-stream with a parameter: the media type takes none.

requests.name: check2_content_type_other
requests.note: Content-Type application/json.

requests.name: check3_key_id_unheld
requests.note: A well-formed key_id the receiver holds for no client, with a valid HMAC under the secret it derives from: the credential is selected by (client_id, key_id), never by trial verification.

requests.name: check3_key_id_of_other_client
requests.note: Client A's request under client B's key_id and a valid HMAC under B's secret: a key_id held for another client selects nothing.

requests.name: check4_hmac_other_secret
requests.note: An HMAC under client B's secret beside client A's key_id.

requests.name: check4_hmac_flipped
requests.note: The right HMAC with its last hexadecimal character changed.

requests.name: check4_hmac_over_other_digest
requests.note: An HMAC computed over another record's digest; the digest header names this body.

requests.name: check4_hmac_raw_secret_key
requests.note: An HMAC keyed with the secret's 32 decoded bytes, not its UTF-8 bytes.

requests.name: check5_skew_past_bound_past
requests.note: sent_at_ms 300001 ms before the receiver's clock: one past the bound.

requests.name: check5_skew_past_bound_future
requests.note: sent_at_ms 300001 ms after the receiver's clock: one past the bound.

requests.name: check5_nonce_reused
requests.note: The (client_id, key_id, nonce) triple is already reserved: a transport replay, although sent_at_ms, the HMAC and the body are fresh.

requests.name: check6_not_canonical
requests.note: The record's members, indented: not the canonical bytes of the object it parses to.

requests.name: check6_unsupported_version
requests.note: A record whose v is 2, signed as such: unsupported_version, a 202 the receiver's state may cure.

requests.name: check6_unsupported_version_max
requests.note: A record whose v is 2^53 - 1, the greatest integer the integer rule admits: unsupported_version.

requests.name: check6_malformed_v_zero
requests.note: A record whose v is 0, signed as such: outside the integer rule, so malformed, never unsupported_version.

requests.name: check6_malformed_v_negative
requests.note: A record whose v is -1: outside the integer rule, so malformed.

requests.name: check6_malformed_v_over_max
requests.note: A record whose v is 2^53, one past the integer rule: malformed.

requests.name: check6_malformed_member_absent
requests.note: A submission observation without its detail member.

requests.name: check6_malformed_kind
requests.note: A record whose kind is neither value.

requests.name: check6_malformed_outcome_delivered
requests.note: A submission observation whose outcome is delivered, a reserved value outside the form.

requests.name: check6_malformed_not_json
requests.note: A body that is not JSON.

requests.name: check6_malformed_not_object
requests.note: A body that is a JSON array holding the record: not one JSON object.

requests.name: check6_malformed_trailing_data
requests.note: The record followed by a second value: not one JSON object.

requests.name: check6_malformed_member_twice
requests.note: The record with v named twice, the second after its last member.

requests.name: check6_malformed_case_variant_member
requests.note: The record with a Device_id member beside device_id: a case variant under the Payload Member Rule's closed fold.

requests.name: check7_device_unknown
requests.note: A record for a device the receiver knows for no client.

requests.name: check7_device_unauthorised
requests.note: A record for a device the receiver knows, but outside this client's set: answered as an unknown device is.

requests.name: check7_device_unauthorised_tally
requests.note: A tally for a device of another client.

requests.name: check7_moved_key
requests.note: The moved device, in the new site's client's set, forwarded by that client under the key enrolled while the device was the old site's: the enrolment names the old owner, never the current one.

requests.name: check7_moved_key_tally
requests.note: A tally from the moved device under its old key, forwarded by the new site's client.

requests.name: check8_key_not_enrolled
requests.note: A record for a device the client may forward for, under a key enrolled for no device: it passes check 7 on the device alone, and check 8 answers key_not_enrolled.

requests.name: check8_key_enrolled_for_other_device
requests.note: A record for device A under device B's enrolled key.

requests.name: check8_key_revoked
requests.note: A record for device A, signed and valid under a key once enrolled for it and since revoked: key_revoked, a 422 no later state cures. The enrolment still names site-a, so check 7 passes.

requests.name: accepted_epochs_apart_attempt_seq
requests.note: The receiver holds device A's record under its current key; this one, under device A's retired key, reuses attempt_seq 41 under another delivery_attempt_id. Within one epoch that breaks consistency, but records under different keys are never judged against each other: stored.

requests.name: accepted_epochs_apart_identity
requests.note: The receiver holds device A's record under its current key; this one has the same delivery_attempt_id and observation_seq under the retired key: an observation's identity is within one epoch, so it is stored, not conflict.

requests.name: check8_signature_invalid
requests.note: A record changed after signing: attempt_seq 43 under the signature over 41.

requests.name: check8_transition_refused
requests.note: observation_seq 2 after a null prior_outcome.

requests.name: check8_class_refused
requests.note: A mandatory tier_d notice with a class.

requests.name: check8_class_refused_tally
requests.note: A tally withheld as disabled with a null class.

requests.name: check8_detail_refused
requests.note: outcome accepted with detail provider_refused: a listed code on another row.

requests.name: check8_signature_over_transition
requests.note: A record changed after signing to observation_seq 2 after a null prior_outcome: Verifying check 4 refuses it before check 5, so signature_invalid wins.

requests.name: check8_key_not_enrolled_over_class
requests.note: A tier_d notice with a class under a key enrolled for no device: Verifying check 3 is first.

requests.name: accepted_conflict_never_earlier
requests.note: The receiver holds a record as stored and another as conflict, the second for reusing the first's attempt_seq under another delivery_attempt_id. A new record of the conflict record's attempt, under another attempt_seq, would break consistency against that record, but a record held as conflict is never the earlier one: it is stored.

requests.name: accepted_conflict_consistency
requests.note: The same new record when the receiver holds the other attempt's first observation as stored: it breaks consistency, attempt_seq differing within one attempt, and is held as conflict, answered stored.

requests.name: accepted_path_first_failed_then_third
requests.note: The receiver holds the attempt's first observation, failed; the incoming record is its third, after accepted: failed ends an attempt, so no legal path has a third observation after it.

requests.name: accepted_path_first_accepted_then_third
requests.note: The receiver holds the attempt's first observation, accepted; the incoming record is its third, after accepted: a third observation follows only an unconfirmed resolved as accepted, so no legal path begins accepted and has three steps; the two are not adjacent, so an adjacent-pair judge misses it.

requests.name: accepted_path_first_unconfirmed_then_third
requests.note: The receiver holds the attempt's first observation, unconfirmed; the incoming record is its third, after accepted: the path unconfirmed, accepted, failed fits both.

requests.name: accepted_path_third_then_first_accepted
requests.note: The receiver holds the attempt's third observation; the incoming record is its first, accepted: no legal path fits both, in whichever order they arrive.

requests.name: accepted_path_second_failed_then_third
requests.note: The receiver holds the second observation, failed after unconfirmed; the incoming third claims accepted before it: conflict.

requests.name: accepted_same_alert_notice_changed
requests.note: The receiver holds one stored observation; the incoming record is another attempt of the same alert_id under another notice, each record valid alone: conflict, answered stored.

requests.name: accepted_same_alert_class_changed
requests.note: The receiver holds one stored observation; the incoming record is another attempt of the same alert_id under another class, each record valid alone: conflict, answered stored.

requests.name: accepted_attempt_seq_reused
requests.note: The receiver holds one stored observation; the incoming record is another delivery_attempt_id under the held attempt's attempt_seq, each record valid alone: conflict, answered stored.

requests.name: accepted_tally_same_count_conflict
requests.note: A tally with the count of one held but different bytes, while a greater count is held for its key: conflict, since one key signed both, answered stored.

requests.name: precedence_1_over_2
requests.note: 33 headers and an upper-case nonce: check 1 is first.

requests.name: precedence_2_over_3
requests.note: A body digest that does not match, under a key_id the receiver does not hold: check 2 is first.

requests.name: precedence_3_over_4
requests.note: A key_id the receiver does not hold and an HMAC under another secret: check 3 is first, and the HMAC is never tried.

requests.name: precedence_4_over_5
requests.note: An invalid HMAC on a request one past the skew bound: check 4 is first.

requests.name: precedence_4_over_5_replay
requests.note: An invalid HMAC on a reused nonce: check 4 is first, so a forged request never consumes or tests a reservation.

requests.name: precedence_5_over_6
requests.note: A stale request whose body is not canonical: check 5 is first, and its response is unauthenticated.

requests.name: precedence_5_over_7
requests.note: A stale request for a device outside the client's set: check 5 is first.

requests.name: check6_unsupported_version_other_device
requests.note: A record of unsupported version for a device outside the client's set: a body that is not a record reaches neither check 7 nor check 8.

requests.name: precedence_7_over_8
requests.note: A record for a device outside the client's set, changed after signing: check 7 is first.

responses.name: row_200_stored
responses.note: The receiver verified the record and holds it durably.

responses.name: row_200_stored_conflict
responses.note: The receiver holds the record as conflict beside another: the response is the same stored, and the gateway retires it.

responses.name: row_200_duplicate
responses.note: The receiver already holds these exact bytes.

responses.name: row_200_superseded
responses.note: A verified tally below the count held: lower_count.

responses.name: row_202_key_not_enrolled
responses.note: The key is not yet enrolled for the device: the receiver's state may cure it.

responses.name: row_202_unsupported_version
responses.note: The record's version is not one the receiver takes yet.

responses.name: row_400_unauthenticated
responses.note: A 400 from check 1 or 2: unauthenticated, exactly v, outcome and an empty reason; the gateway keeps the record and never rejects it.

responses.name: row_400_not_canonical
responses.note: An authenticated 400 from check 6, bound to the request's digest: reject, to the audited rejected store.

responses.name: row_400_malformed
responses.note: An authenticated 400 from check 6, malformed, bound to the request's digest: reject.

responses.name: row_401_refused
responses.note: Transport authentication failed: unauthenticated, it omits record_digest; the gateway keeps the record and repairs its credential.

responses.name: row_403_not_owned
responses.note: The authenticated client may not forward for this device: keep, under the bounded hold, and never retire.

responses.name: row_422_key_revoked
responses.note: Verification fails for a reason no later state cures: key_revoked.

responses.name: row_422_signature_invalid
responses.note: Verification fails for a reason no later state cures: signature_invalid.

responses.name: row_422_transition_refused
responses.note: Verification fails for a reason no later state cures: transition_refused.

responses.name: row_422_class_refused
responses.note: Verification fails for a reason no later state cures: class_refused.

responses.name: row_422_detail_refused
responses.note: Verification fails for a reason no later state cures: detail_refused.

responses.name: row_429_retry_later
responses.note: A rate limit, with Retry-After.

responses.name: row_503_retry_later
responses.note: The receiver cannot commit durably.

responses.name: another_digest_stored
responses.note: 200 stored naming another record's digest.

responses.name: another_digest_duplicate
responses.note: 200 duplicate naming another record's digest.

responses.name: another_digest_400
responses.note: An authenticated 400 malformed naming another record's digest: the gateway does not reject.

responses.name: another_digest_422
responses.note: 422 signature_invalid naming another record's digest: the gateway does not reject.

responses.name: unparsable_truncated
responses.note: A 200 body cut short.

responses.name: unparsable_empty
responses.note: A 200 with an empty body.

responses.name: unparsable_text
responses.note: A 200 with a body that is not JSON.

responses.name: unparsable_not_object
responses.note: A 200 whose body is a JSON array, not the response object.

responses.name: unparsable_extra_member
responses.note: 200 stored with a fifth member: neither form's members.

responses.name: unparsable_v_2
responses.note: 200 stored with v 2.

responses.name: unparsable_outcome_absent
responses.note: 200 with no outcome member.

responses.name: unparsable_outcome_unknown
responses.note: 200 with an outcome outside the table's vocabulary.

responses.name: unparsable_digest_upper
responses.note: 200 stored naming the request's digest in upper-case hexadecimal: not of the digest's form.

responses.name: unparsable_stored_with_reason
responses.note: 200 stored with a reason that is not empty.

responses.name: unparsable_422_reason_outside
responses.note: 422 refused whose reason is not one of the four.

responses.name: unparsable_400_reason_empty
responses.note: A 400 that names the request's digest but carries no reason: an authenticated 400 carries check 6's reason.

responses.name: unparsable_429_reason
responses.note: 429 retry_later whose reason is not empty: a 429 carries only an empty reason.

responses.name: unparsable_503_reason
responses.note: 503 retry_later carrying key_not_enrolled: a 503 carries only an empty reason.

responses.name: unparsable_202_reason_empty
responses.note: 202 retry_later with an empty reason: a 202 carries check 6's or 8's reason.

responses.name: unparsable_unauthenticated_reason
responses.note: A 401 of three members whose reason is not empty: the unauthenticated form carries only an empty reason.

responses.name: unpaired_200_refused
responses.note: 200 with outcome refused: in form, but the table pairs neither.

responses.name: unpaired_200_retry_later
responses.note: 200 with outcome retry_later.

responses.name: unpaired_202_stored
responses.note: 202 with outcome stored.

responses.name: unpaired_201_stored
responses.note: 201 with outcome stored: a status the table does not hold.

responses.name: unpaired_422_retry_later
responses.note: 422 with outcome retry_later.

responses.name: unpaired_400_stored
responses.note: 400 with outcome stored.

responses.name: unpaired_500_refused
responses.note: 500 with outcome refused: a status the table does not hold.

responses.name: unparsable_three_members_200_stored
responses.note: 200 stored of exactly v, outcome and an empty reason: the unauthenticated form is only refused, at 400 or 401.

responses.name: unparsable_three_members_422
responses.note: 422 refused of three members: the unauthenticated form is only a 400 or 401, so the gateway keeps and never rejects.

responses.name: unparsable_three_members_403
responses.note: 403 refused of three members: a 403 is authenticated and names the digest.

responses.name: unparsable_three_members_401_retry_later
responses.note: 401 of three members with outcome retry_later: the unauthenticated form's outcome is refused.

responses.name: unparsable_three_members_400_stored
responses.note: 400 of three members with outcome stored.

responses.name: unpaired_200_retry_later_empty
responses.note: 200 retry_later with an empty reason: in form, and the table pairs 200 with no retry_later row.

responses.name: unpaired_429_stored
responses.note: 429 stored with an empty reason: in form, and the table pairs 429 with no stored row.

responses.name: unpaired_403_retry_later
responses.note: 403 retry_later with key_not_enrolled.

responses.name: order_another_digest_over_unpaired
responses.note: 200 refused naming another record's digest: another digest is classed before unpaired.

responses.name: order_another_digest_over_reason
responses.note: 422 refused with a reason its row does not name, naming another record's digest: another digest is classed before the reason.

responses.name: order_unpaired_over_reason
responses.note: 200 retry_later with a reason no row names: unpaired is classed before the reason.

responses.name: order_form_over_another_digest
responses.note: 200 stored with v 2 and another record's digest: the form is classed first.

responses.name: order_unauthenticated_parsed_not_bytes
responses.note: A 401 in the unauthenticated form with insignificant whitespace and its members in another order: judged as the JSON it parses to.

responses.name: row_200_stored_parsed_not_bytes
responses.note: 200 stored with whitespace and its members out of order: judged as the JSON it parses to, and retired.

responses.name: unparsable_429_unauthenticated_form
responses.note: 429 retry_later of three members: a 429 is sent only once checks 1 to 5 have passed, so it names the digest; in the unauthenticated form it does not parse.

responses.name: unparsable_503_unauthenticated_refused
responses.note: 503 refused of three members with an empty reason: the unauthenticated form is a 400 or 401 only.

responses.name: unauthenticated_400_check2
responses.note: A 400 refused in the unauthenticated form, as a request refused at check 2 is answered: keep, never reject.

responses.name: unauthenticated_401_check5
responses.note: A 401 refused in the unauthenticated form, as a replayed request is answered: keep.

config.name: accepted_base
config.note: Enabled, a separate absolute queue, three distinct well-formed forwarding names, none shared with another credential's variable.

config.name: accepted_custody_without_forwarding
config.note: Enabled with none of the three forwarding keys: custody is configured without forwarding.

config.name: accepted_forwarding_keys_all_empty
config.note: All three forwarding keys present and empty: none is present and not empty, so custody is configured without forwarding.

config.name: accepted_forwarding_keys_absent_and_empty
config.note: endpoint_env empty, the other two absent: no forwarding.

config.name: accepted_lowercase_dotted_names
config.note: Names in lower case with dots and hyphens: rules 6 to 8 impose no pattern beyond White_Space and `=`.

config.name: accepted_shared_endpoint_and_client_names
